_llm_instructions: Fill in the 'project_title' and 'date_prepared' properties, and the 'value' property of each field, based on the provided project context. Reference parameters.md for global project variables.

f01_ID.label: ID
f01_ID.guidance: A unique identifier. Keep it short, stable, and never reused, because the same ID appears in the trace from vision to release and a reassigned ID breaks that trace without anyone noticing.

f02_Summary_Description.label: Summary Description
f02_Summary_Description.guidance: A brief description of the requirement or need, in no more than one or two sentences. If it needs a paragraph, the item is probably two items, or it belongs in the vision rather than the backlog.

f03_Priority.label: Priority
f03_Priority.guidance: A way of ranking the requirements. Either summary groups such as high, medium, and low, or a numbered rank. State which scheme is in use, because a backlog that mixes the two cannot be sorted.

f04_Story.label: Story
f04_Story.guidance: A prioritised user story, or the name of a user story recorded elsewhere. Where the story lives elsewhere, reference it rather than copying it, so the two do not diverge.

f05_Status.label: Status
f05_Status.guidance: Whether the requirement is not started, in progress, or complete. Use the same set of values for every row, since a status column with mixed vocabularies cannot be filtered.

f06_Story_Points.label: Story Points
f06_Story_Points.guidance: Estimating information such as story points. An estimate is a prediction made to compare against actuals, so record it even when it is a rough guess, and do not revise it silently.

f07_Target_Sprint_or_Release.label: Target Sprint or Release
f07_Target_Sprint_or_Release.guidance: Which sprint or release the item will be incorporated into. Treat this as a forecast: an item that keeps moving between releases is telling you something, and the churn is worth seeing.

f08_User_Type.label: User Type
f08_User_Type.guidance: The user type that will benefit, such as customer, administrator, or manager. This is what shows which parts of the organisation the release actually serves.

f09_Category.label: Category
f09_Category.guidance: A category, which helps on large projects where the backlog is too big to hold in one view. Categories should reflect how the work is actually sequenced, not how the team happens to be divided.
